title: What We Know About Psychotherapy - Objectively and Subjectively
coreMove: Hold external evidence and inward experience together without forcing one to pretend it is the whole truth.
sourcePressure: Rogers asks what psychotherapy knowledge looks like from outside measurement and from inside lived experience, refusing to let either mode erase the other. Frozen sidecar ch04 supports the heading, part placement, and broad thematic claims; it exposes no chapter-local named anecdotes, studies, or places.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Making the chapter a science-versus-feelings argument.
sourceAnchorNote: The frozen source exposes no usable chapter-local named person, study, institution, place, date, or anecdotal artifact from Rogers here. Use fictional protagonists only; do not invent named Rogers cases or studies.

hook: opening with a definition of objective knowledge
counterintuition: Most people think X, but Y
It is not about being nice
The paradox is that acceptance changes everything
